## speed-sol2-small: a cached root goal ~10x its bound: look the global cache up before building the EvalCtxt (solver-sync speed-of-light section 6)

- Where: `vendor/rustc_next_trait_solver` `evaluate_root_goal` (`solve/eval_ctxt/mod.rs`): every root goal builds an `EvalCtxt` and a search-graph frame, runs the proof-tree builder's no-op checks and instantiates the response, even when the answer is in the global cache. rustc's profiles put that at several hundred ns; the bound is ~100 cycles (canonicalize with no infer vars = one flag test, intern hit, cache lookup, nothing to instantiate).
- Change: a patch in the series (`PATCHES.md`, replayed by `tools/v2/solver_sync.py`): for a root goal whose canonical input has no inference variables, look it up in the global cache first and return the cached response directly when it has no variables to instantiate; else the path as today. Same answers (the cache is what the full path would read first).
- Proof: proof's budget "a cached root goal": time per goal and allocations (0). Measure before applying, once the tree builds; the patch should also go upstream.
